chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Jimmy Harrison, the trombonist who influenced others
summary: Jackson names Harrison first among trombone influences, saying many stole from him including Benny Morton and Teagarden.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Well, let's get back to our era now and start bringing the trombone players up.
Who basically really influenced you beside -- of course, you say your brother-in-law, Claude Jones, which was married to your sister.
And who were some of the great guys you admired, great trombone players, of that era, Butter?
Jimmy Harrison. Tell me about him. Elucidate.
Jimmy Harrison was -- he could do more with five notes than any trombone player I ever heard. He was
a great swing trombone player. He would make you pat your foot. There was a lot of guys that, I think, stole from him. I have to say they stole from him.
I tell you, the closest to me that played like him was -- oh, Bennie Morton was one of them.
And Teagarden used to listen to him, too, you know. And the trombone player that was with Chick. I think even he played as nearest, I'll call his name.
